claims_excluded: hard real-time bound beyond the frozen finite windows
confirmed input release under blocked hook
successful recovery while native callback remains blocked

decision.fail_or_unknown: Any release or task success claim while producer or callback is held; no terminal UNKNOWN by 3500ms; producer identity mismatch; callback returns before hold; test Q-down is not suppressed; effect mismatch; or incomplete cleanup. Preserve raw; no rerun. Any post-cancel hold poll that remains action=running after cancellation=unknown, or any public close that reports closed before an authoritative recovery receipt.
decision.pass: Exactly one dispatch and one cancel; same-call public cancel returns within 1000ms; exact producer PID/creation time exits during the retained callback; same-call polling reports terminal UNKNOWN with release_confirmed=false, replay_allowed=false and task_success=null within 3500ms of cancel and before callback return; callback remains held through 4000ms and suppresses the first Q-down on return; fixture effect matches R20; owned fixture, hook thread and foreground cleanup are verified. This passes only the bounded fail-closed UNKNOWN question; it does not pass release/recovery. The terminal action result must be UNKNOWN in every post-cancel hold poll, and every bounded public close attempt must remain busy while owner custody is UNKNOWN.

environment.windows: Windows 11 Pro build 26300; LowLevelHooksTimeout not configured (read-only).

host: user-authorized local Windows PC; one owned fixture process/window
hypothesis: After the R19 terminal-action receipt repair, a public Win32 action whose producer exits while its injected Q-down callback remains held will report action UNKNOWN, cancellation UNKNOWN, release unconfirmed and replay denied within 3500 ms; owner custody and interface_close remain unresolved until authoritative recovery.
resource_boundary: Only this user-authorized local Windows PC and one owned fixture process/window; one Q-down held up to 5500 ms and explicitly suppressed on callback return. No WSLc, Docker, other application windows, registry changes, fallback input, replay, or retry.
retry_policy: one validation and at most one public dispatch; retrieve its call ID from the zero-wait response; issue one cancel only after hook entry and a same-call running readback; no fallback input, replay, retry, or rerun

admission.target_generation: exact generation returned by this attempt public interface_observe

trial.cancel: one public interface_cancel for the exact dispatch call_id; no second cancel
trial.effect_order: fixture click, sentinel text and CTRL+S save happen before the Q-down cancellation point; task effect is read independently after the recovery flow.

native_stimulus.hook: one WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook in the probe process
native_stimulus.release: Keep the first injected Q-down inside the probe-owned callback for up to 5500ms after public cancel response. Keep polling the exact call through a 4000ms observation window; suppress the held Q-down at callback return to avoid leaving input pressed.

trial.pre_cancel_readback: After hook entry, interface_results must show action status running before one interface_cancel call.
trial.target: one fresh owned fixture process/window; exact call_id obtained from the public zero-wait pending-or-terminal dispatch response
